en.one: A German company that sells its own CAD/CAM software and distributes Autodesk products. It passed the walls, but nine-month profit fell and it pays out more than it earns.
en.business: Mensch und Maschine runs two businesses. The Software segment sells engineering software it develops itself (for example Open Mind's hyperMILL); in 2025 it had revenue of 114.5 million euros, operating profit of 32.4 million euros and an operating margin of 28.3%. The Digitization segment distributes Autodesk software and provides training and customisation; in 2025 its gross profit was 79.1 million euros and operating profit 16.7 million euros. Group gross profit in 2025 was 181.9 million euros and net profit 31.8 million euros; it has 1,192 employees.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. Evidence: its own software brings about two thirds of operating profit (32.4 million of 49.1 million euros in 2025) at a margin of 28.3%; changing engineering software means retraining and data migration for the customer. Real return on equity averaged 29.6% over five years and was 21.6% in its lowest year. Gross profit from own software rose 8.5% in the first nine months of 2026 and operating profit 18%. Why not wide: the other segment depends on another company's product, and that company sets the terms. In the last quarter of 2024 Autodesk moved its partners from resale to commission; group revenue fell 27% in 2025, and in the first nine months of 2026 the Digitization segment's gross profit fell 12.5% and its operating profit 38%. According to the company, the Autodesk business is less than 25% of group gross profit. For pricing power we looked at the gross margin in the inflation years: the group gross margin was about 52% in 2023 and 53.6% in 2024 (our arithmetic); the 76.2% of 2025 shows the switch of Autodesk revenue to commission, not price increases. So pricing power cannot be read from the margin.
en.mgmt: Founder and chairman Adi Drotleff holds 48.38% of the shares; other managers 5.36%, free float 42.27%, treasury shares 3.98% (31 December 2025). The company's policy is to pay out all of its profit: a dividend of 2.00 euros per share was proposed for 2025, when earnings per share were 1.91 euros, so the payout exceeds profit. For 2026 it plans 2.20-2.40 euros. In 2025 it also bought back 657,686 shares for 31.5 million euros; the average price was 47.83 euros, well above today's price (32.8 euros). The result: cash fell from 43.0 million to 15.8 million euros, bank loans rose from 5.3 million to 33.3 million euros, and equity fell from 104.9 million to 84.8 million euros. Part of the payout was therefore funded with debt; this is why the D score is 1. Goodwill is 47.9 million euros (56% of equity); there were no new acquisitions in 2025, only purchases of minority stakes in two subsidiaries. Share-based pay is small: the employee share plan cost 0.2 million euros. The pension obligation is 2.3 million euros and covered by plan assets; lease liabilities are 13.6 million euros. Loans of 2.5 million euros come from the main shareholder and his family. Contingent liabilities and recurring one-off charges: checked, not in the document.
en.latest: 20 October 2026: The company published its nine-month results. Revenue was 189.3 million euros (+6.9%), gross profit 135.0 million euros (−0.5%), operating profit 36.9 million euros (−0.7%), net profit 23.4 million euros (−3.7%) and earnings per share 1.42 euros (1.45). Operating profit in Software rose to 29.1 million euros (+18%); in Digitization it fell to 7.8 million euros (−38%). Third-quarter earnings per share were 0.31 euros (0.39 a year earlier; the difference between nine months and the first half). The company kept its 2026 target of 11-19% growth in earnings per share (2.11-2.26 euros) but said it can only reach the lower half, and only with a strong fourth quarter. It expects no further drag from Autodesk from 2027.
risks: The price calculation assumes the company holds its profit; yet earnings per share fell 2.2% in the first nine months of 2026 and about 20% in the third quarter. Meeting the annual target needs a clear jump in the fourth quarter (the low end of the target is 2.11 euros; nine months gave 1.42 euros).
Autodesk can change its partner terms unilaterally; the model change of 2024-2026 cut the Digitization segment's profit by 38%. A new change could do the same.

The company pays out more than it earns and buys back shares; in 2025 bank loans rose to 33.3 million euros and equity fell to 84.8 million euros. Part of the rise in return on equity comes from the shrinking equity.
Customers are in cyclical sectors such as machinery, automotive and construction; in an investment slump, sales of new licences and services slow.
Buybacks were made at an average of 47.83 euros; the share is now at 32.8 euros. Management's aim of earnings per share above 3.80 euros in 2030 is a target, not a commitment.

WSU.moat_text: Hendek dar sınıfta. Şirketin kendi araştırmasına göre WashTec dünya pazar lideridir; kurulu makine sayısı 43.500'ü aşar ve Avrupa'da pazar payı farkı büyüktür. Yıllık rapora göre pazara giriş engeli yüksektir, çünkü yaygın bir servis ağı ve kurulu makine tabanı gerekir; kurulu her makine yıllarca servis ve kimyasal geliri getirir. Reel özsermaye kârlılığı beş yılda ortalama %28,6, en düşük yılında %18,6. Neden geniş değil: fiyatlama gücü marjda görünmüyor. Brüt marj 2024'te %31,0, 2025'te %31,3; faaliyet kâr marjı %10 dolayında kaldı ve 2026'da şirket %8-9 bekliyor. Kuzey Amerika'da kârlılık düşük (2025 faaliyet kâr marjı %3,6; Avrupa %10,9). Büyük müşteriler küresel akaryakıt şirketleridir; çerçeve sözleşmeler yeniden ihaleye çıkar ve şirket bunu fiyat baskısı riski olarak yazar. Yüksek özsermaye kârlılığının bir nedeni de ince özsermayedir (30 Haziran 2026: 58,5 milyon avro, bilançonun %20'si). Brüt marjın 2021-2023 seyri okunan bölümlerde yok.
WSU.mgmt: Hâkim ortak yok; en büyük ortaklar fonlardır: EQMC (Alantra) %15,14, Morgan Stanley %10,61, Kempen Oranje Participaties %9,60, Norman Rentrop %7,13 (31 Aralık 2025). Şirket kârından fazlasını dağıtıyor: 2025 için hisse başına 2,50 avro temettü, hisse başına kâr 2,29 avro; 2024 için 2,40 avro, kâr 2,32 avro. en.one: World market leader in car wash equipment; its service network and installed base are the moat. It passed the walls, but profit is falling in 2026 and the dividend exceeds earnings.
en.business: WashTec sells car wash machines to fuel stations and wash operators, services those machines and supplies wash chemicals. Revenue in 2025 was 498.6 million euros: equipment 268.0, service 155.1 and consumables 69.6 million euros. Service and consumables, the recurring part, were 45.1% of revenue. Europe and other regions brought 425.5 million euros and North America 75.5 million euros. Operating profit in 2025 was 48.9 million euros (9.8%) and net profit 30.7 million euros.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. According to the company's own surveys WashTec is the world market leader; its installed base exceeds 43,500 machines and its lead in market share in Europe is large. The annual report says barriers to entry are high because a dense service network and an installed base are needed; each installed machine brings years of service and chemical revenue. Real return on equity averaged 28.6% over five years and was 18.6% in its lowest year. Why not wide: pricing power does not show in the margins. The gross margin was 31.0% in 2024 and 31.3% in 2025; the operating margin has stayed near 10% and the company expects 8-9% in 2026. Profitability in North America is low (2025 operating margin 3.6%; Europe 10.9%). The large customers are global oil companies; framework contracts are re-tendered and the company lists this as a risk of price pressure. Part of the high return on equity also comes from thin equity (30 June 2026: 58.5 million euros, 20% of the balance sheet). The gross margin for 2021-2023 is not in the sections read.
en.mgmt: There is no controlling shareholder; the largest holders are funds: EQMC (Alantra) 15.14%, Morgan Stanley 10.61%, Kempen Oranje Participaties 9.60%, Norman Rentrop 7.13% (31 December 2025). The company pays out more than it earns: a dividend of 2.50 euros per share for 2025 against earnings per share of 2.29 euros; 2.40 euros for 2024 against 2.32 euros. The result: equity fell from 88.5 million euros at the end of 2024 to 58.5 million euros on 30 June 2026; net financial debt was 52.2 million euros at the end of 2025 (2024: 46.3). No profit is retained; growth investment is funded with debt and operating cash. This is why the D score is 1. Treasury shares: 627,809 (4.49%); a buyback of up to 100,000 shares or 5.0 million euros began in November 2025, and 1.5 million euros was spent in 2025. Goodwill is 43.8 million euros, about three quarters of end-June equity. On 14 September 2026 the management board was cut to two members and the chief executive's contract was extended to April 2030. Restructuring charges recur: costs of the chief executive change in 2024 and a single-digit million euro amount for organisational changes in 2026. Personnel provisions (including pensions) are 10.6 million euros; lease liabilities 22.6 million euros. The amount of share-based pay and contingent liabilities: checked, not in the sections read.
en.latest: 3 November 2026: Nine-month results were published (figures from a press report; the company's statement could not be opened). Revenue was 374.5 million euros (+4.6%), operating profit 25.7 million euros (−20.7%; margin 6.9% against 9.0% a year earlier), net profit 16.1 million euros (21.1) and earnings per share 1.21 euros (1.57). In the third quarter operating profit fell to 8.0 million euros (14.8 a year earlier). Free cash flow was 8.6 million euros (27.8); working capital rose. Special expenses of 2.0 million euros were booked for organisational changes. On 14 September 2026 the company had cut its 2026 guidance: an operating margin of 8-9% (2025: 9.8%) and a return on capital employed below last year's; mid-single-digit revenue growth is kept. The reasons: delays in the production relocation and installation cost projects, and consumables sales below expectations.
risks: The price calculation rests on the profit of the last 12 months, and profit is falling. Earnings per share fell 23% in the first nine months of 2026 and roughly halved in the third quarter, and the company cut its margin guidance for the year to 8-9%. According to the company, the gains from its efficiency programmes have slipped by a year.

The dividend exceeds earnings; equity has fallen to 58.5 million euros, 20% of the balance sheet. The same dividend cannot be sustained while profit falls; the 8% dividend yield in the data rests on last year's payment of 2.50 euros.
Equipment sales depend on customers' investment decisions and are cyclical; real return on equity fell to 18.6% in 2022. Order intake in the nine months was below last year and declined in Europe.
Large oil companies can re-tender their framework contracts; if a rival gets listed, revenue and prices come under pressure. A figure for customer concentration is not in the document.
The North American arm has been low-margin for years (3.6% in 2025) and the company is investing more there; if it does not pay off, the return on capital falls.

Müşteri yoğunlaşması ve kamunun hasılattaki payı: bakıldı, okunan belgelerde rakam yok. Fiyat artışlarının kanıtı da okunan belgelerde yok.

Haziran 2025'te Oblivation'ın kalan %49'u eski yönetimden alındı; satıcılar arasında ilişkili bir taraf vardı, bedel okunan belgede yok. Bu yüzden D puanı 1. Hisse bazlı ücret programı yok (eski opsiyon programlarından 0,3 milyon avro yedek duruyor). en.one: An Austrian company selling electronic records and document management software to public bodies. It passed the walls; 61% of revenue recurs, but the company itself calls the first half's profit strength temporary.
en.business: Fabasoft develops the software that public bodies and companies use for electronic files, documents and process management; it sells cloud services, licences and project services. In the fiscal year to March 2026 revenue was 90.0 million euros, operating profit 15.7 million euros (17.4%) and net profit 10.8 million euros. Recurring revenue was 54.9 million euros (61.0%). It spends 29.4% of revenue on research and development and has 505 employees. In the April-June 2025 quarter about 44% of revenue came from Germany, 39% from Austria and 10% from Switzerland (our arithmetic).
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The company describes itself as the market leader in electronic records in the German-speaking countries. For a public body, replacing its records and workflow system means a migration that takes years; this ties the customer in. Evidence: recurring revenue grew 12.5% in 2025/26 and its share of revenue rose from 56.2% to 61.0%; the operating margin rose from 15.3% to 17.4%. Real return on equity averaged 24.0% over five fiscal years and was 14.4% in its lowest year; as the company has net cash, this return does not rest on debt. Why not wide: the company is small (revenue of 90 million euros) and far larger software companies work in the same field; 39% of revenue still comes from non-recurring project and licence work won through public tenders. Customer concentration and the public sector's share of revenue: checked, no figure in the documents read. Evidence of price increases is also not in the documents read.
en.mgmt: The main shareholder is the founders' foundation, Fallmann & Bauernfeind Privatstiftung; its percentage is not in the documents read. Founder Helmut Fallmann chairs the managing board. The dividend is uneven: 0.10 euros per share for 2024/25 and 0.50 euros for 2025/26 (annual meeting of 8 July 2026; earnings per share 0.97 euros). The company holds 223,627 treasury shares (about 2.0%); there were no recent buybacks. Cash is 35.8 million euros (30 September 2026; 41.8 million on 31 March 2026); the only significant debt is a 12 million euro, 15-year loan taken in October 2024 for an office building. Profit goes mostly into the product. There are minorities in subsidiaries: the company owns 85.5% of Mindbreeze. In June 2025 the remaining 49% of Oblivation was bought from its former management; the sellers included a related party, and the price is not in the document read. This is why the D score is 1. There is no share-based pay programme (0.3 million euros remains in reserves from former option plans). Goodwill, pension deficit and contingent liabilities: checked, not in the documents read; lease liabilities were 5.9 million euros (30 June 2025).
en.latest: 13 November 2026: The company reported the April-September 2026 half-year. Revenue was 51.5 million euros (43.6 a year earlier; +18%), recurring revenue 31.2 million euros (26.1; 60.6% of revenue), EBITDA 15.0 million euros (11.1), operating profit 10.9 million euros (7.3) and the operating margin 21.3% (16.8%). Cash flow from operations was 7.0 million euros (0.8). According to press reports the result for the period was 7.8 million euros (5.1) and earnings per share 0.72 euros (0.44); the half-year report itself could not be opened. In the July-September quarter operating profit was 5.6 million euros (4.9). Personnel expenses rose 6.9%, more slowly than revenue; headcount was 493 (497). The company calls the strength in operating profit temporary: marketing spending, hiring and investment were delayed. There is no numerical guidance.
risks: The profit of the last 12 months includes a very strong first half: in April-September 2026 earnings per share rose from 0.44 to 0.72 euros (press report). The company calls this strength temporary; profitability will fall once the delayed marketing, hiring and investment spending is made. If this half-year is taken as normal earning power, value looks higher than it is.

Most customers are public bodies in Austria, Germany and Switzerland; a budget cut or the loss of a large framework contract hits revenue directly. A figure for customer concentration is not in the documents read.
39% of revenue is project and licence work that moves from quarter to quarter; profit is uneven as a result (real return on equity was 14.4% in 2021/22 and 30.2% in 2023/24).
Far larger software companies offer cloud and AI products to the same public customers; 29.4% of revenue goes to research and development, and the return on that spending is not certain.
The company is based in Austria and the shares trade in Frankfurt; the inflation adjustment uses the inflation of the listing country (Germany).

LIK.business: Limes Schlosskliniken, tarihî yapılarda ve dinlenme bölgelerinde özel psikiyatri ve psikosomatik klinikleri işletir. Hastalar çoğunlukla özel sigortalı, kendi ödeyen, memur yardımı alan ve yurt dışından gelen kişilerdir. Almanya'da dört kliniği, İsviçre'de Paracelsus Recovery (payı %56) ve Lihtenştayn'da Clinicum Alpinum (payı %51) vardır; toplam altı tesis, yaklaşık 400 tedavi yeri. 2025'te satış geliri 50,0 milyon avro, FAVÖK 12,8 milyon avro (%23,7), ana ortaklık kârı 5,7 milyon avro; 52.374 hasta günü.
LIK.moat_text: Hendek zayıf; şirket 3. suru bu yüzden geçemedi (B = 1). Üstünlük var: klinikler dolunca kârlılık yüksek (2025 FAVÖK marjı %23,7), reel özsermaye kârlılığı beş yılda ortalama %36,1. Ama bu üstünlüğün kalıcı olduğunu gösteren kanıt okunan belgelerde yok. Şirket günlük ücretlerini, doluluk oranını ve fiyat artışlarını açıklamıyor; fiyatlama gücü rakamla gösterilemiyor. İş, bina kiralayıp ruhsat alan başka işletmecilerce de kurulabilir; büyüme yeni klinik açmakla gelir ve her yeni klinik yıllarca düşük dolulukla çalışır: 2025'te açılan Abtsee için 2026'da ortalama %56, Bergisches Land için %40 doluluk varsayılıyor. Yeni yatırımlarla reel özsermaye kârlılığı 2021'deki %82,5'ten 2024'te %14,7'ye inmiş, 2025'te %27,9 olmuştur. Tablolar Alman muhasebe yasasına (HGB) göre tutulur.
LIK.mgmt: GMF Capital GmbH payların %75,64'ünü tutar; halka açık pay %24,36. Hisse Düsseldorf borsasının serbest pazarında kotedir; açıklama yükümlülükleri düzenlenmiş pazardan azdır ve ara dönem tabloları denetimden geçmez. 2025 için temettü önerisi okunan raporda yok. 2026'nın ilk yarısında ortaklara ve azınlık pay sahiplerine 4,7 milyon avro ödendi (geçen yıl 0,2 milyon avro); dökümü okunan özette yok. İlişkili taraf: genel müdür, iki kliniğin müdürlüğü için 2025'te hâkim ortak GMF Capital üzerinden 59.500 avro aldı; ortaklara borç 0,5 milyon avro. Hisse bazlı ücret önemli: genel müdüre 2018-2024 için 11.000 pay söz verilmiş ve henüz verilmemiş (toplam 297.952 payın yaklaşık %3,7'si); ayrıca 1.600 opsiyon var. Şerefiye net 6,8 milyon avro (2025 sonu), on yılda itfa ediliyor; özsermaye 26,8 milyon avro. Banka borcu 10,7 milyon avro, nakit 10,3 milyon avro (2025 sonu). Uzun süreli kira taahhütleri var ama tutarı açıklanmıyor; kira ve bina gideri 2025'te 5,6 milyon avro. Ertelenmiş vergi bilançoya alınmıyor.
LIK.latest: 31 Ağustos 2026: Şirket ilk yarı sonuçlarını açıkladı (denetimden geçmemiş). Satış geliri 29,7 milyon avro (23,0), FAVÖK 7,0 milyon avro (6,2), faaliyet kârı 5,0 milyon avro (4,9), ana ortaklık kârı 3,1 milyon avro (3,3), hisse başına kâr 10,49 avro (11,30). Hasta günü 31.552 (+%17,5); çalışan sayısı 314 (237). Kâr, iki yeni kliniğin açılış giderleri yüzünden hasılat kadar artmadı. Şirket ikinci yarıda Mecklenburgische Schweiz kliniğinde havuz arızası yüzünden daha zayıf bir gidiş bekliyor. İtalya'da Villa Boccella'nın alımı sürüyor; açılış 2027 yazında bekleniyor. Yıllık raporda 2026 için yaklaşık 66 milyon avro hasılat ve 15-18 milyon avro FAVÖK öngörülmüştü.
risks: Hendek zayıf: fiyatlama gücünü gösteren rakam yok ve özel sigortaların ödeme kuralları değişirse gelir doğrudan etkilenir.
Büyüme yeni klinik açmaya bağlı; yeni klinikler yıllarca düşük dolulukla çalışır ve sermayenin getirisini düşürür. 2026'nın ilk yarısında hasılat %29 artarken ana ortaklık kârı %6 geriledi.
Hâkim ortak payların %75,64'ünü tutuyor; hisse serbest pazarda ve sığ işlem görüyor, ara dönem tabloları denetlenmiyor. Genel müdüre söz verilen 11.000 pay verilince ortakların payı sulanır.

Uzun süreli kira taahhütlerinin tutarı açıklanmıyor; bu bilanço dışı bir yükümlülüktür. Şirketin bir bölümü İsviçre ve Lihtenştayn'da çalışır; enflasyon düzeltmesi borsanın ülkesine (Almanya) göre yapılmıştır.

en.one: It runs mental health clinics for privately insured and self-paying patients. Profitable and growing, but we judged the moat weak; it failed Wall 3.
en.business: Limes Schlosskliniken runs private psychiatric and psychosomatic clinics in historic buildings and resort areas. Patients are mostly privately insured, self-paying, civil-service aid recipients and international clients. It has four clinics in Germany, Paracelsus Recovery in Switzerland (56% owned) and Clinicum Alpinum in Liechtenstein (51% owned): six sites in all with about 400 treatment places. In 2025 sales revenue was 50.0 million euros, EBITDA 12.8 million euros (23.7%) and profit attributable to the parent 5.7 million euros, on 52,374 patient days.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak; this is why the company failed Wall 3 (B = 1). There is an advantage: once clinics fill up, profitability is high (2025 EBITDA margin 23.7%), and real return on equity averaged 36.1% over five years. But the documents read hold no evidence that this advantage lasts. The company does not disclose its daily rates, occupancy or price increases; pricing power cannot be shown with numbers. Other operators can also lease a building, obtain a licence and set up the same business; growth comes from opening new clinics, and each new clinic runs at low occupancy for years: for Abtsee, opened in 2025, average occupancy of 56% is assumed for 2026, and 40% for Bergisches Land. With the new investments, real return on equity fell from 82.5% in 2021 to 14.7% in 2024 and was 27.9% in 2025. The accounts follow the German Commercial Code (HGB).
en.mgmt: GMF Capital GmbH holds 75.64% of the shares; the free float is 24.36%. The shares are listed on the open market of the Düsseldorf exchange; disclosure duties are lighter than on a regulated market and interim accounts are not reviewed by an auditor. A dividend proposal for 2025 is not in the report read. In the first half of 2026, 4.7 million euros was paid to owners and minority shareholders (0.2 million euros a year earlier); the breakdown is not in the summary read. Related party: in 2025 the chief executive received 59,500 euros through the controlling shareholder GMF Capital for managing two clinics; liabilities to shareholders are 0.5 million euros. Share-based pay is significant: the chief executive has been promised 11,000 shares for 2018-2024 that are not yet delivered (about 3.7% of the 297,952 shares); there are also 1,600 options. Net goodwill is 6.8 million euros (end of 2025), amortised over ten years; equity is 26.8 million euros. Bank debt was 10.7 million euros and cash 10.3 million euros (end of 2025). There are long-term rent commitments but their amount is not disclosed; rent and premises costs were 5.6 million euros in 2025. Deferred taxes are not recognised.
en.latest: 31 August 2026: The company published its first-half results (unaudited). Sales revenue was 29.7 million euros (23.0), EBITDA 7.0 million euros (6.2), operating profit 5.0 million euros (4.9), profit attributable to the parent 3.1 million euros (3.3) and earnings per share 10.49 euros (11.30). Patient days were 31,552 (+17.5%); employees 314 (237). Because of start-up costs at the two new clinics, profit did not grow with revenue. The company expects a weaker second half at the Mecklenburgische Schweiz clinic because of a pool malfunction. The purchase of Villa Boccella in Italy is in progress; opening is expected in summer 2027. The annual report forecast revenue of about 66 million euros and EBITDA of 15-18 million euros for 2026.
risks: The moat is weak: there is no figure showing pricing power, and revenue is hit directly if private insurers change their reimbursement rules.

Growth depends on opening new clinics; new clinics run at low occupancy for years and lower the return on capital. In the first half of 2026 revenue rose 29% while profit attributable to the parent fell 6%.

The controlling shareholder holds 75.64%; the shares trade thinly on the open market and interim accounts are not audited. Delivery of the 11,000 shares promised to the chief executive will dilute shareholders.

The amount of long-term rent commitments is not disclosed; this is an off-balance-sheet liability. Part of the business is in Switzerland and Liechtenstein; the inflation adjustment uses the inflation of the listing country (Germany).
